name: Granite 4.0 H Tiny
attention_variant: GQA on 4 of 40 layers; Mamba-2 on 36; NoPE
notes: MoE + hybrid-Mamba, and both matter. config.json layer_types gives 40 layers of which 36 are 'mamba' and only 4 are 'attention' (positions 5, 14, 23, 32). num_local_experts 64 with num_experts_per_tok 6 and a shared_intermediate_size 1024 always-on expert alongside per-expert hidden 512. params_b 6.939 is the safetensors total; active_params_b 1.0 is IBM's own stated active-parameter figure for H-Tiny in the model card table, NOT derived from config - treat as vendor-stated. KV: only the 4 attention layers hold KV. bf16 KV bytes/token = 4 attention layers x 4 KV heads x 128 head_dim (1536 / 12) x 2 x 2 bytes = 8192 B/token = 8.0 KiB/token - 16x smaller than the 131,072 B/token of a 32-layer 8B dense GQA model (Llama-3.1-8B geometry), and 5.5x smaller than Falcon-H1-7B's 45,056 B/token, the only other hybrid in this slice. The ranking across this slice is: 8,192 B/token (Granite 4.0 H-Tiny) << 16,384 (Nemotron-H-8B) << 45,056 (Falcon-H1-7B) << 114,688 (Falcon3-7B) < 131,072 (Llama-3.1-8B) << 163,840 (Granite 3.3 8B) - i.e. the hybrid-Mamba models buy a 8-16x KV reduction over comparable dense GQA models, but only the interleaved 4-attention-layer variants get it; Falcon-H1's parallel-in-every-layer design gets barely 2.9x. The other 36 layers carry a constant Mamba-2 state instead: mamba_d_state 128, mamba_d_head 64, mamba_n_heads 48, so per sequence per layer the recurrent state is 48 x 64 x 128 = 393216 elements = 0.75 MiB at bf16, x 36 layers = 27 MiB, constant in context length. Net: KV does not grow with context, and resident state is a one-time 27 MiB per sequence. position_embedding_type 'nope' - NoPE on the attention layers, with Mamba carrying position implicitly. mamba_chunk_size 256, mamba_d_conv 4. Serving shape: 6.9B of weights resident (the memory bottleneck) for 1B of per-token compute (the speed bottleneck), 131072 native context with no rope_scaling.
